product.text: the life cycle of a sea turtle, from egg to adult

start.text: a nest of eggs buried in the sand

end.text: the return of adult females to the beach where they hatched

st1.text: a female digs a nest in the sand and lays about 100 eggs

st2.text: the eggs are warmed by the sun for about 60 days

st3.text: the hatchlings emerge at night and crawl to the sea

st4.text: drift in the open ocean for five to ten years, feeding on small animals

st5.text: they move into shallow coastal waters as sub-adults and eat seagrass and jellyfish

st6.text: the turtles mature at 20 to 30 years of age and the females return to their home beach to lay eggs

rating.strength: "the females return to their home beach to lay their own eggs, so the cycle starts again" closes the cycle exactly as the diagram does.
